meta.purpose: Researched inputs for the Phase 3 low-confidence snapshot builder (historical-basemaps polities, 3000 BCE to 1994). Every numeric leaf is an Est {low, mid, high, grade, source, note}; derived:* methods are documented in data/SOURCES.md, section "Phase 3 derivation inputs".
meta.yearRule: Keys are the historical-basemaps file years between 3000 BCE and 1994 (bc1 = -1). For a snapshot year between two keys interpolate linearly (log-linearly for populationDensity); before -3000 use -3000, after 1994 use 1994.
meta.regionRule: RegionId of the polygon centroid. regionCountries lists the modern countries (ISO3) whose HYDE/Maddison series make up each region: the project nations.json region where the nation exists, else the World Bank region mapping of data-pipeline/generate-modern.ts, plus GRL -> north_america and a few territories assigned by geography. Countries without a land area (TWN, ESH, Kosovo, small territories) are left out of the density sums.

historical.formula: factor = exp(intercept + slope * ln(clamp(areaKm2, areaClampKm2)) + regionOffset[region]); stateDensity = populationDensity[region][year].mid * factor; population = areaKm2 * stateDensity. mid uses intercept.mid; low/high use intercept.low/high with slope and offset at mid (intercept low/high carry the residual quartiles).

intercept.note: OLS of ln(snapshot density / regional HYDE density) on ln(areaKm2) over 133 researched pre-1991 snapshots; residual sd 0.80; low/high = intercept + residual quartiles (-0.43 / 0.52). Use low/high for the snapshot low/high.

slope.note: OLS slope +/- 1 standard error (0.041). Negative: small polities are denser than their region, large empires include empty land.

cyber.note: frontier anchor curve at 1994 CE (piecewise linear between the Tech level anchors in data/SOURCES.md); no regional lag unless tech.regionalCaps applies. +/-0.3 judgement band.

weapons.note: https://www.nber.org/system/files/working_papers/w12657/w12657.pdf sec. 2.1: New World peoples did not use bronze until near European contact; coded without bronze or iron weapons in 1000 BC and 0 AD, without firearms in 1500 (Table 2 variables). Stone/obsidian and copper = anchor 0-1.

armor.note: inference from the same metallurgy finding (no bronze/iron): padded/leather armour, anchor 0-1. Not coded by CEG.

ships.note: https://m.nber.org/data-appendix/w12657/appen.pdf transport section: no compass and no ocean-traversing or warfare-capable armed ships before contact; canoes = anchor 0-1.

logistics.note: https://m.nber.org/data-appendix/w12657/appen.pdf: the wheel and animal-drawn vehicles reached the New World only after contact; porters (anchor 0), Andean llama trains at most 1.

communications.note: https://m.nber.org/data-appendix/w12657/appen.pdf communications: no paper, books or printing; Inca oral society, writing only in Mesoamerica. Runners/relays = anchor 1.

regionalCaps.appliesTo: indigenous polities only (not colonial or post-independence states)
regionalCaps.caps: same caps as the pre-1493 entry, grade D: CEG measures the pre-contact state only; adoption of horses and firearms after contact varied by polity.

weapons.note: https://www.nber.org/system/files/working_papers/w12657/w12657.pdf Table 4: Oceania has the lowest overall technology adoption in every period (0.20 in 1000 BC, 0.17 in 0 AD, 0.12 in 1500 AD, vs Europe 0.66/0.88/0.87). Stone weapons = anchor 0-1.

armor.note: no metallurgy (same CEG Table 4 basis); anchor 0-1, inference.

ships.note: Pacific voyaging canoes exceed the anchor-0 raft but carried no armament; judgement, not coded by CEG.

logistics.note: no draft animals or wheel; porters = anchor 0. Inference from CEG Table 4.

communications.note: no writing; runners and signal fires = anchor 0-1. Inference from CEG Table 4.

weapons.note: https://www.nber.org/system/files/working_papers/w12657/w12657.pdf sec. 2.2 and appendix: iron used throughout Africa by 1500 but no steel in Sub-Saharan Africa before European contact; Songhai and others coded without firearms. Iron weapons and cavalry, no gunpowder: between anchors 3 and 4.

armor.note: no steel (CEG): iron mail and quilted armour at most, anchor ~3. Inference.

ships.note: https://m.nber.org/data-appendix/w12657/appen.pdf: no ocean-traversing ships, compass only on the East African coast; river and coastal craft = anchor 1-2.

logistics.note: https://m.nber.org/data-appendix/w12657/appen.pdf: wheel introduced by European settlers (Ethiopia and Morocco uncertain); pack animals and porters = anchor 1.

regionalCaps.caps: ships and logistics caps of the 500-1500 entry, grade D; weapons and armor uncapped because firearms spread through West and East Africa after 1500 (no fetched source quantifies the lag).

weapons.note: https://www.nber.org/system/files/working_papers/w12657/w12657.pdf sec. 2.1: China first used iron in the 6th century BC, so bronze weapons (anchor 2-2.5) until then.

tech.rule: tech[field] = min(default[year][field], cap[field]) for every regionalCaps entry whose regions include the polity region, fromYear <= year <= toYear and appliesTo matches; grade of the result = the grade of whichever term is used. Where the default is used, also cap at the polity's own documented equipment if the builder knows it.

bronze.reason: Mycenaean and Danubian palace/warrior elites fought from chariots with infantry levies.

iron.reason: Celtic, Italic, Iberian and Greek states fought with infantry levies; the profile names them.

medieval.reason: Mounted men-at-arms plus levies raised by obligation; 8 of 9 researched European medieval snapshots use it.

gunpowder.reason: Standing drilled armies fighting in line; 9 of 12 researched European gunpowder snapshots.

industrial.reason: Conscription, reserves and railways; 9 of 10 researched European industrial snapshots.

worldwars.reason: Remaining (smaller) European states lacked the industry to mechanise; the great powers are researched already.

coldwar.reason: Most remaining European states were NATO or neutral; use archetype-coldwar-soviet for Warsaw Pact members if the builder knows the bloc.

modern.reason: Remaining 1994 European polities are small states facing larger neighbours; 4 researched precedents.
